applies_to: Vector Controls X2 family controllers fitted with the CS2-BAC-001 BACnet IP (Ethernet / Wi-Fi) communication module.
summary: The X2 BACnet IP module exposes the same core objects as the MS/TP module (controller state, inputs, loops, outputs, fans, alarms) plus the twelve time schedules as objects and fan lead-lag timers. Objects only appear for the I/O the specific X2 product has.
notes: Objects are created only for the inputs, outputs, loops and alarms the X2 product actually has; the datasheet scope table says which exist.
Digital output objects depend on how each output is configured (fan, 3-point floating, PWM or binary); the same instance can appear in several of these tables, listed here once.
Alarm MVs (601-608) can only be written to Not Active when the alarm is waiting for confirmation.
Other controller parameters are reached through ParAdd/ParValue (an address + value pair), not as separate objects.
Each of the 12 time schedules has TYPE, NR (group ID) and DAYS MVs and TIME and SP AVs; in holiday mode the same schedule uses the HDAY/HMONTH start/end AVs.
Object names in the controller-state block differ from the MS/TP module (e.g. MV 0 Occupation instead of OpStCoSt), and ParAdd/ParValue are AV 0/AV 1 here.

integration.summary: Use BV 0 for on/off and MV 0 for occupancy, write loop set points (AV 211 for loop 1) and read inputs, loop outputs and alarms. Time schedules can be set over BACnet through the TS objects.
integration.enable: BV 3-7 lock or unlock local access to modes, set points, manual control, heat/cool change and time programs.
integration.heartbeat: Virtual inputs (AV 109-116) set to the communication module must be rewritten within the controller's timeout, or the input and its functions are disabled.
integration.remote_sensors: Write sensor values to the virtual inputs VI-01..VI-04 (AV 109, 111, 113, 115) when they are set to the communication module.
setup: IPv4 address and DHCP on/off are set in the controller's COM parameters.
